international.title: Burnham sets three tests for EU deal, saying it should make Brexit ‘closer to what people thought they were voting for’ – UK politics live
international.summary: PM to address fallout from Brexit in speech this evening Burnham to say Brexit ‘has not worked’ At her press conference, Kemi Badenoch faced various questions about Brexit, and Andy Burnham’s reset deal with the EU. She dismissed Burnham’s plan to debate a closer relationship as a “distraction”. Here are some of her arguments. Badenoch said Burnham’s deal with the EU was just a “big nothingburger” until the details were published, and she repeatedly described his call for a debate on the future relationship with the EU as a “distraction”. She said: Andy Burnham is not the one who started this EU reset. Quite a lot of what Keir Starmer went and did at the last EU reset has not come to pass … People have forgotten, but all he managed to do was give away our fish. Everything else is still unsettled. So the fact is Labour going to the EU and talking about a big reset moment is a big nothingburger until we see what’s come back and when it’s actually implemented. Badenoch backed David Cameron’s argument that the problems facing Britain have nothing to do with Brexit. She said: Andy Burnham still has not learned the lessons of the past. He is still living in 2016. The problems that this country faces today have nothing to do with being in or out of the EU. France was literally on fire last month. It’s in the EU. It has a small boat crisis, as do many other European countries. They are in the EU. She said Burnham wanted the opposition to talk about Brexit “because if we’re talking about that, then we’re not talking about the government’s failures” . She added: “I’m not falling for that trick.” She said she agreed with Boris Johnson when he told the Daily Telegraph that, in a second referendum, people would again vote to be out of the EU. Asked about his comments, she said: I wasn’t an MP when we had the referendum. And I remember everyone assuming that remain would win and all the polls and stats showed remain winning. And then something different happened. So all of the people bringing out stats and polls saying people would vote to go back into the EU – I would ask them to go and look at the news from ten years ago and familiarise themselves with that. She refused to say whether she would support or oppose the deal Burnham is set to agree on Friday. She said: I speak as a former trade secretary. [Burnham] laid out all of his negotiating tactics and all of his asks [before agreeing the EU deal]. You never, ever do that when you’re negotiating because the other party can squeeze out more concessions. Take something like youth mobility, for instance. I support youth mobility depending on the conditions. I negotiated youth mobility for countries like Australia … The issue is not youth mobility. It’s what are the terms that are going with it? When I was 16, I remember reading the Peter Stringfellow case, a 55-year-old man dating a 16-year-old, and I thought it was the most disgusting thing ever. I do think ... that there’s some common sense there in terms of a staggered age of consent. My issue is with how we will enforce it. Politicians need to focus on building capacity, building prison spaces, renting spaces abroad, which is one of our policies, rather than creating more laws that cannot be enforced … [The government is] all over the place. Let’s have an age of maturity and stick to it, and let’s have some coherence in policy. Continue reading...
